steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Night shift left two kegs from the same dump. Function names already match. provenance.json host rows wander between kegs, and one listing grows extra source suffixes. Desk mill is /app/bin/ashquay (native ELF). splice CORE OUTDIR reads a dump under /app/dumpit, wells under /app/dbgwells, cards under /app/cardurn, then writes backtrace.txt and provenance.json under the OUTDIR argument. Grade kegs: /app/outkeg/runA and /app/outkeg/runB. That means /app/outkeg/runA/backtrace.txt, /app/outkeg/runA/provenance.json, /app/outkeg/runA/ok.mark, /app/outkeg/runB/backtrace.txt, /app/outkeg/runB/provenance.json, and /app/outkeg/runB/ok.mark. Line grammar: /app/vatnotes/forms.txt. Desk notes: /app/vatnotes/BAYMAP.txt. Provenance objects rows carry build_id and host.

Do /app/dumpit/shift.core twice, once into each keg. Trees must be byte-identical. Clean splice writes ok.mark. A dump whose id no well holds exits non-zero and leaves ok.mark missing.

C pipeline modules named in /app/vatnotes/BAYMAP.txt require source code fixes under /app. Static copies of the outkeg files are not enough. The verifier reruns /app/bin/ashquay splice /app/dumpit/shift.core /app/outkeg/runA.

steps.message:
Analysis: Current splice succeeds and creates ok.mark, but repeated runs are not byte-identical: runB adds `src/z.c:3` to the final frame while runA does not. A shared `/app/outkeg/poll.log` also appeared, suggesting stateful host selection/contact logging outside each output directory. Provenance happened to match this time but the task warns host rows wander. We need inspect the C modules named by BAYMAP, build configuration, dump/well/card formats, and notes to find unstable selection and source-suffix logic.
Plan: Read all source/header/build/config/note files and inspect fixture bytes/content. This should reveal pipeline ownership, ordering, mutable state, and intended card/well behavior. Then patch only the responsible modules, rebuild the native ELF, and test repeated clean runs plus a fabricated unknown-ID dump if its format is clear.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/millcue/*.[ch] /app/millcue/hull.mk /app/hopbag/*.[ch] /app/objbay/*.[ch] /app/ribvat/*.[ch] /app/sidelog/*.[ch] /app/mill.cfg /app/vatnotes/ops.txt; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,240p' "$f"; done
for f in /app/cardurn/*.card /app/dbgwells/*/*.dbg /app/dumpit/*.core; do echo "===== $f ====="; file "$f"; xxd -g1 "$f" | head -80; done
echo '--- symbols/modules ---'; nm -an /app/bin/ashquay | grep -E ' (main|splice|op_|pick|well|credit|retry|write|render)' || true; echo '--- build dry run ---'; make -C /app/millcue -f hull.mk -n

steps.message:
Analysis: The visible code exposes two definite defects. `op_bag` returns only one host and chooses it based on whether OUTDIR contains `A`, directly making output-directory names affect object selection. `n_credit` ignores each selected object's actual host and writes `retry_first` for every row. The varying source suffix likely comes from differing debug objects selected by this host logic. We still need the omitted `n_pick`/`readwell` code and fixture text to determine the intended deterministic ranking/contact order and whether source rows should come from the selected object.
Plan: Print the previously truncated source modules and all text fixtures using `cat`. Then patch host enumeration/selection and provenance based on actual ranking semantics. Also review cleanup behavior: stale ok.mark must be removed before processing so failed reruns cannot leave a success marker.

for f in /app/cardurn/*.card /app/dbgwells/*/*.dbg /app/dumpit/*.core; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The intended deterministic pipeline is now clear. All wells must be queried, then `n_pick` must choose deterministically by card rank rather than OUTDIR spelling. Rank 1 makes deepwell the selected source for both IDs, so the stable backtrace includes deepwell's line record for `baz`. Provenance must report each selected object's real host, not overwrite it with `retry_first`. The retry setting should affect contact order only. Finally, ok.mark must be removed before every attempt so a failed rerun cannot retain an old success marker.
Plan: Replace `op_bag` so it returns every card host in deterministic contact order, with `retry_first` first and remaining hosts ordered by rank/name. Implement `n_pick` as lowest-rank selection with a lexical host tie-break. Fix `n_credit` to emit selected hosts. Update main to remove ok.mark before processing. Rebuild, run twice, compare trees byte-for-byte, verify exact files/content, then create an unknown-ID core and confirm nonzero exit with no ok.mark.
